Ellie Goulding has such a huge catalog of songs that I genuinely cannot believe we've made it this far without a single one being used for a Drag Race lipsync.

And somehow this bothers me more than Halsey never getting a lipsync song despite being a guest judge on Season 10 Episode 2 "PharmaRusical". 😭

Like...**how have we gotten THIS far and still no Ellie Goulding??**

“Lights,” “Burn,” “Anything Could Happen,” “Love Me Like You Do,” “On My Mind,” “Starry Eyed,” “Goodness Gracious”...there are SO many possibilities.

I need to know what Ellie song you guys think would make the best lipsync. My answer would be "Still Falling For You"

And if anyone who picks the lipsync songs on Drag Race UK is watching, **please take note.** 😭

text:
Makayla Couture and her attempt to be a villain

Anyone else feel that Makayla trying to be a villain/shady feels off for her actual personality? Like she was trying to be a "bad bitch" for TV but her actual personality was nicer than that?

  
For example when Juice Boxx was talking about wanting to be a father and Makayla was like "awwww I hope you get it" the energy was so genuine and sweet from her, it felt so much more authentic than some of the times she's tried to be shady. 

  
Likewise apparently she cried multiple times trying to do choreo in the girl group challenge, which seems more like a sensitive person who hates conflict rather than someone who loves to cause conflict.

  
Anyone else feel the same? I feel like she created this character for the TV because some queens have stayed longer because of villain edits, but it just doesn't seem to fit her that well. 

  
I'm not claiming to know her off the show I'm just talking about the times she's shown what seems to be an inner sweetness and sensitivity on the show underneath the "I'm a bad bitch" character on the show itself.

text:
Why are queens who don't know how to sew (or even hold a hot glue gun) still auditioning for Drag Race

We all agree Drag Race casts those queens to make drama and storylines (mentoring, stressing over a dress, etc) and because they have other amazing skills besides making a dress or a personality that works for TV.

However, for a queen to get into the finals, she must survive the 2 to 3 design challenges so knowing  the basics to make a dress to be safe at least in those episodes is a must.

Drag Race is basically universal among the queens in the US, and there are many unspoken rules and protocols (such as not removing your heels unless your lipsync is out of this world). So why after 17 years and tons of sewing challenges, the queens are still daring to audition without knowing how to sew, and if they make the cut, are surprised thay they have to sew in a challenge.

text:
What episode 12 did right.

Episode 11 was frustrating because during the seminar performances, it would cut to confessionals where queens would tell us who was doing well and who was bombing. This was frustrating. It wasn't even accurate. While Plane Jane and Q were saying, "Doctor, doctor!", it cut to Morphine saying, "Doctor, doctor! This is funny." But it wasn't. Plane Jane and Q had other funny moments in their performance, but the "Doctor, doctor!" part wasn't one of them.

Episode 12 eliminated this problem. The viewers got to see every bathroom presentation without it cutting to confessionals. This was so refreshing. After watching all three presentations, the audience was able to draw their own conclusions about who did well and who struggled. Thank you, Drag Race. I don't need commentary from queens to push me in a certain direction.
label: analysis

text:
This forced Onya hate is far too much

**\^ She won right here btw \^**

**I think as a community we need to come together and stop all dog piling and l hate Onya is constantly receiving, we’re already hated by many why hate on one of our own who doesn’t deserve it. She’s a talented queen and proved this during her run, yet the fans feel the need to discredit her at every opportunity they can.** 

**It’s sad to see the way she’s talking about her fellow sisters on podcasts, it can be seen as playful shade but it does feel like honesty from her. I’ve not seen many queens defending her win, probably to stay on the right side of certain fans. And what Lana said honestly upset me to see that she feels they had a bond.** 

**The last time a winner was this bullied by fans was Tyra, and look how that turned out, Tyra didn’t even have the same about of exposure Onya has and social media wasn’t as big and hateful during her reign. I know Onya is a stronger person than Tyra, but constant undeserved hate can change a person mentally.** 

**Jewels who I really loved on the season was in no way winning, Onya bodied that season with only Suzie coming second to her (and yes was rigged to be eliminated by production and should have been in that finale with Onya.)**

**This comes down to one thing and one thing alone, the blatant racism in the drag race fandom, who for some reason manages to push their agenda far more than the actual fans of the show. And if she’s just not your cup of tea leave it there without fuelling the fire.** 

**Also the backlash Arietty faced was minuscule to the extent Onya has faced, and she said and did some awful things on and off the show.**
